title: U.S. House · Michigan's 9th District
area: Michigan's 'Thumb' region and northern Macomb County, including Romeo, Rochester and St. Clair, Sanilac and Lapeer counties.

context.text: Incumbent Lisa McClain (R) advanced unopposed from the Republican primary. Ray Pooley (D) won the Democratic primary.

candidates.name: Lisa McClain
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2021); House Republican Conference Chair

summary.text: Lisa McClain is the Republican incumbent, seeking re-election. She chairs the House Republican Conference, the fourth-ranking position in House GOP leadership.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from Northwood University.
Founded and worked as president of North End Support Team before entering Congress.
Elected chair of the House Republican Conference in the 119th Congress.

record.text: Assigned to the Committee on Financial Services and the Committee on Education and the Workforce for the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Chaired the Health Care and Financial Services subcommittee of the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform in the 118th Congress (2023-2024).
Elected chair of the House Republican Conference for the 119th Congress, the fourth-ranking position in House Republican leadership.

candidates.researchNotes: No 2026 campaign statements or Candidate Connection survey responses were found describing McClain's current policy positions beyond her committee record; her campaign website's public pages did not list detailed issue positions.

summary.text: Ray Pooley is a machinist making his first run for Congress, campaigning on manufacturing jobs, family farms and Medicare for All.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Hartland High School.
Career experience includes working as a machinist.

priorities.text: Bringing manufacturing back to the U.S. and protecting the right to unionize.
priorities.quote: We will unleash American ingenuity to bring jobs home... We will ensure these new jobs pay a living wage by protecting the right to organize and join a union.

priorities.text: Supporting family farms against large agribusiness.
priorities.quote: It's time to break the grip of global conglomerates on our food supply. We will empower family farmers with the tools and knowledge for healthy soil, regenerative practices...

priorities.text: Medicare for All and expanded childcare services.
priorities.quote: I will fight to break the corporate monopolies on healthcare to ensure every American has the freedom to access quality, affordable care... through Medicare For All.

positions.quote: ...providing the security and peace of mind you deserve through Medicare For All.

positions.summary: Supports providing childcare services for all families.
positions.quote: ...we have the means and capability to provide childcare services for all, and therefore the responsibility to do so.

positions.summary: Supports raising the minimum wage alongside a cap on the ratio between CEO and worker pay.
positions.quote: ...raising the minimum wage while putting a maximum ratio for CEO pay...

positions.summary: Supports simplifying the tax code so that higher earners pay more and closing corporate tax loopholes.
positions.quote: That means simplifying the tax code so the ultra-wealthy pay their fair share, allowing us to cut taxes for working families, as well as closing all the tax loopholes these corporations take advantage of.

positions.summary: Supports domestic solar and wind power development over reliance on foreign oil.
positions.quote: By harnessing American-made solar, wind, and other innovative technologies, we can produce abundant, cheap, and clean power right here at home.

positions.summary: Opposes what he calls 'un-American ICE raids' while supporting a secure border and a faster legal immigration process.
positions.quote: End un-American ICE raids and enforce smart border policy, targeting root cause.
